## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet, so nothing is ruled out in this world. Earlier worlds suggest that when every score is 0, the world differs from its description. The likeliest difference is the action or mask layout, and recipe changes never helped. Hedging the layout was the only thing that ever worked (world 2, about 0.22). Since 1x1 convs see all channels at once, they already handle any order of the obs channels. So obs-order bets only matter for spatial changes (transposes and flips). This round runs the reference net unchanged as an anchor, plus five layout bets: a 16-layout hedge (8 grid symmetries × type-major or type-minor order), that hedge with a 5x5 head conv, a hedge for DONE being at index 0, a hedge for the obs being transposed or flipped relative to the mask, and a dense Linear path that can handle any layout. All use the world-2 recipe so the networks are the only difference. If any run shows nonzero training success, I'll follow it.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0, both on dev and on training success. They used the same recipe as world 2's success, so this world deviates in some other way. Ruled out, at least as the only cause: any of the 8 grid symmetries between the obs and the action layout (the 16 output layouts cover them all), type-major vs type-minor order, DONE at index 0, anchors or footprints within ±2 cells, obs channel permutations (1x1 convs see every channel), and a mismatch in action count (the starting net would have crashed). Still untested: an obs stored channel-last but read channel-first, input scaling (no normalisation anywhere), obs cells scrambled spatially, dynamics that need per-layer landing reasoning, value gradients swamping the shared trunk, and reward or horizon issues that collapse exploration. Each candidate below targets one of these. Most also include cheap hedges (16 layouts, GroupNorm), so that any nonzero result is a signal.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0, in training and on dev. Their parameter counts match the stated spec exactly (r1c1 has 53,130 parameters, which needs T=4, 8x8 and C=27), so the shapes are as described. The deviation must be in layout or behaviour. Already tested and still 0: the 8 grid symmetries with type-major or type-minor order, DONE first, obs flips and transposes, channel-last obs, a bottlenecked dense mask or obs embedding, a GN stem, a separate critic, a per-layer head and an exploration recipe. Still untested: (a) action orders with the type axis in the middle (Y,T,X or X,T,Y), which no earlier hedge covered; (b) any fixed permutation of actions or cells, which needs full-rank remaps (earlier dense paths went through 64-wide bottlenecks or were zero-initialised); (c) non-local dynamics, such as sliding, that need a global receptive field; (d) 180° or 90° rotations between obs groups. Every candidate uses the 24-layout set (6 axis orders × 4 flips).

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. This rules out the following explanations, each tested in at least one trial: an action layout from any of the 6 axis orders × 4 flips (24 layouts); DONE at index 0; obs transposed, flipped, in any of the 8 symmetries, or read channel-last; any fixed cell or action permutation (full-rank remaps); scale problems in a shared GN stem; no global context (mixer); value interference; a per-layer landing head; 5x5 footprints; and moderate horizon or entropy changes. In world 2, the layout hedge was what turned 0 into 0.22, so this world's deviation is probably not about layout. The remaining suspects are dynamics within the grid plane, mask channels that add noise or drown out the obs, an input-scale imbalance between obs and mask, a DONE trap or entropy collapse under different rewards, and learning simply being too slow at this budget. This is the last round, so each candidate makes one distinct structural bet. Any of them may also change the recipe in support of that bet.
